topic.name: Factoring Sums and Differences of Cubes

question.explanation:
The sum of cubes formula is given by \[ a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2). \]

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $3.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $3,$ as follows: \[ 81n^3 + 24 = 3\left( 27n^3 + 8 \right) \]

The expression in parentheses can be written as a sum of cubes: \[ 3\left( 27n^3 + 8 \right) = 3\left( (3n)^3 + 2^3 \right) \]

Now, we factor the expression in parentheses using the sum of cubes formula:

\begin{align} 81n^3 + 24 &= 3\left( (3n)^3 + 2^3 \right) \\[3pt] &= 3(3n + 2) \left( (3n)^2 - 3n \cdot 2 + 2^2 \right) \\[3pt] &= 3(3n + 2) \left( 9n^2 - 6n + 4 \right) \end{align}

topic.name: Factoring Sums and Differences of Cubes

question.explanation:
The difference of cubes formula is given by \[ a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2). \]

Notice that we can write our expression as a difference of cubes: \[ \dfrac{x^3}{8} - \dfrac{z^6}{125} = \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^3 - \left( \dfrac{z^2}{5} \right)^3 \]

Now, we factor the given expression using the difference of cubes formula:

\begin{align} \dfrac{x^3}{8} - \dfrac{z^6}{125} & = \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^3 - \left( \dfrac{z^2}{5} \right)^3 \\[5pt] & = \left(\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{z^2}{5} \right)\left(\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{x}{2}\cdot \dfrac{z^2}{5} + \left( \dfrac{z^2}{5} \right)^2\right) \\[5pt] & = \left(\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{z^2}{5} \right)\left(\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{x z^2}{10} + \dfrac{z^4}{25}\right) \end{align}

example.title: Factoring Sums and Differences of Cubes with Fractional Terms

question.explanation:
The sum of cubes formula is given by \[ a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2). \]

Notice that we can write our expression as a sum of cubes, as follows: \[ 8 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} = 2^3 + \left( \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^3 \]

Now, we factor our expression using the sum of cubes formula: \begin{align} 8 + \dfrac 1 {x^3} & = 2^3 + \left( \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^3 \\[5pt] & = \left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x} \right) \left(2^2 - 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} + \left( \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^2\right) \\[5pt] & = \left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x} \right) \left(4 - \dfrac{2}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) \\[5pt] \end{align}
